title: OPQ Protocol Document Structure — Standard Sections
summary: An Operational and Performance Qualification (OPQ) protocol follows a standard structure that satisfies 21 CFR Part 11 and GAMP 5 requirements. This template is applicable to any Salesforce-based life sciences application.

front_matter.signature_page: Approval signatures from QA, System Owner, Process Owner, and Validation Lead certifying the protocol is authorized for use. Minimum 3 signatories. Document status tracking (New → Revised → Retired).
front_matter.table_of_contents: Full TOC with page numbers for all sections and attachments.

section_1_introduction.1.1_objective: State the purpose: gather and document evidence that the system has been installed and operates in accordance with URS and FDA 21 CFR Part 11.
section_1_introduction.1.2_scope: Define which modules/features are in scope. List specific functional areas being tested (e.g., sample delivery, inventory, returns, transfers, reporting). Include sub-sections for Exclusions (what is NOT being tested and why), Assumptions (about test environment, data, training), Test Environment (which org/sandbox), and Pre-requisites (training, environment readiness, user profiles).
section_1_introduction.1.3_description: Brief system description — what it does, SaaS/hosted model, key features.

document_structure.section_2_roles_and_responsibilities: Define who writes the protocol, who executes it, who reviews results, and who approves. Typically a joint effort between the customer organization and a validation consultancy. QA must be independent.
document_structure.section_3_approach: State the testing methodology — user tests and functionality tests based on configured paths. Reference applicable regulations: 21 CFR Part 11, FDA General Principles of Software Validation, GAMP 5.
document_structure.section_4_definitions: Standardized terms: Approval, Commissioning, CRM, Equipment, FDA, Qualification, Quality, SOP, System, URS, Workflows.
document_structure.section_5_references: Cross-reference documents: URS, System Functional Specifications, User Guides for each user role.
document_structure.section_6_execution_instructions: How to execute the protocol: expected vs actual results, signature requirements, corrections protocol (single-line cross-out, initial, date), handling of critical system changes during validation.
document_structure.section_7_acceptance_criteria: Operation/performance must match design intent. All yes/no answers must be 'yes'. Actual results must match expected results or be satisfactorily explained.
document_structure.section_8_exception_resolution: How deviations are documented and resolved. Cross-reference to Corrective Action Form (appendix).
document_structure.section_9_summary_report: After testing, results feed into the Validation Summary Report (VSR). Same approvers or qualified designees sign off.

test_attachments_pattern.format: Each functional area is a numbered attachment with: Test Objective → Test Method → Results Table → Comments → Acceptance Criteria → Sign-off
typical_attachments_for_sample_managemen: Signature Verification List — personnel executing the protocol
Test Equipment — equipment used in qualification that is not part of the system
Audit Trail Verification — print before, execute, print after, compare
Screen Navigation — verify all UI screens are designed and connected as required
Virtual Transfer Request — functional operations for VTR
Acknowledgment of Delivery (AOD) — data load verification, edit/submit workflows
Physical Inventory — submission and reconciliation workflows
Adjustment Request — submission and approval workflows
Acknowledgment of Transfer (AOT) — transfer receipt and confirmation

appendices: Corrective Action Report — form for documenting protocol deviations, required actions, risk assessment, and resolution
Corrective Action Log — running log of all deviation numbers, test sections, pages, and dates

title: OPQ Test Script Design Patterns — How to Write Effective Test Steps
summary: OPQ test scripts follow specific patterns to ensure reproducibility, traceability, and regulatory compliance. Each step must be unambiguous enough for a trained user to execute without interpretation.

navigation_verification.purpose: Verify that the user interface screens are designed and connected as required
navigation_verification.pattern: Access [page/view] → Verify [specific elements/sections] are displayed → Navigate to [sub-section] → Verify [expected content]
example_steps: Access the Home Page View → The following functional sections will be displayed: Pending Items, Samples Distributed, AOT, Returns, Reports
Select the Samples Dispensed tab → Transactions for Samples Dispensed are displayed
Verify user role determines which tabs/sections are visible

data_entry_and_submission.purpose: Verify that data entry, validation, and submission workflows operate correctly
data_entry_and_submission.pattern: Navigate to [form] → Enter [specific test data] → Verify [field behavior/validation] → Submit → Verify [result/confirmation]
example_steps: Select AOD tab → AOD detail page is displayed
Enter delivery quantity: 100 → Field accepts value
Submit the form → Confirmation message displayed, record saved
Verify submitted record appears in the list view with correct values

audit_trail_verification.purpose: Verify that the system maintains a complete, immutable audit trail
audit_trail_verification.pattern: Print audit trail BEFORE test → Execute operations → Print audit trail AFTER → Compare the two printouts → Verify new entries capture who/what/when
critical_checks: Audit trail contains history of changes from all operations performed
Audit trail does NOT contain decrypted passwords
Old and new values are captured for modified fields
User identity is recorded for each change

data_load_verification.purpose: Verify that ETL/data load processes produce correct results
data_load_verification.pattern: Screenshot BEFORE load → Execute data load → Screenshot AFTER load → Verify data load information matches source → Verify record counts and field values

edit_and_update_workflows.purpose: Verify that existing records can be modified through defined workflows
edit_and_update_workflows.pattern: Open existing record → Modify [specific fields] → Save → Verify changes saved correctly → Verify audit trail captures the change

test_data_conventions: Data to be entered may be enclosed in quotation marks in the protocol (e.g., Enter 'quotes' in the Sample field)
Lengthy numeric fields may include commas for legibility (e.g., 99,999,999.9999) — commas are not entered during execution
Pre-requisite test data should be loaded via ETL or manual setup BEFORE test execution begins
Test environment must contain representative data — not production data unless anonymized
execution_rules: Each protocol section signed and dated by the person(s) completing it
Handwritten corrections: single line cross-out, initial, date
Critical system changes during validation must be reported in the final summary report
Changes after completion of the final report documented through formal change control
gotcha: Test steps must be PRESCRIPTIVE, not descriptive. 'Verify the system works correctly' is NOT a valid test step. 'Navigate to the AOD tab, enter quantity 100 in the Delivery Quantity field, click Submit, and verify the confirmation message displays the submitted quantity of 100' IS a valid test step. Each step must have an objectively verifiable expected result.

title: OPQ Acceptance Criteria and Deviation Management
summary: Every OPQ attachment must have explicit acceptance criteria, and any failure to meet those criteria triggers a deviation that must be formally documented, classified, and resolved.

acceptance_criteria_patterns.standard_pattern: All actual results are the same as the expected results or satisfactorily explained
acceptance_criteria_patterns.signature_verification: Signature verification is complete and signed by the individuals executing this protocol
acceptance_criteria_patterns.equipment_list: Equipment that is not part of the system being qualified but used in this qualification is listed
acceptance_criteria_patterns.workflow_tests: All actual results match expected results. Any 'No' answer must be documented as a deviation.

corrective_action_report_fields: Protocol Attachment Number — which test section
Page Number — where the deviation occurred
Protocol Requirements — state what the protocol required
Deviation Description — state what actually happened vs. what was expected
Investigation/Corrective Action — root cause analysis and corrective steps taken
Risk Assessment — impact on system validation and GxP compliance
Signatures — person completing, reviewer, QA approval

deviation_classification.Critical: GxP-critical function does not work as required — blocks go-live until resolved
deviation_classification.Major: Function works but with significant limitation or workaround — must be resolved within defined timeline
deviation_classification.Minor: Cosmetic or non-GxP issue — can be resolved in future release

sample_management_system.total_test_steps: 600-700 for a medium-complexity module with 8-10 functional workflows
sample_management_system.test_attachments: 10-12 (one per functional area plus audit trail and navigation)
sample_management_system.typical_deviation_rate: 5-15% of test steps may generate deviations on first execution

gotcha: Every deviation MUST be classified, investigated, and formally closed — even minor ones. An unresolved deviation in the protocol is a regulatory finding waiting to happen. Inspectors specifically look for open deviations in the Corrective Action Log.

title: Sample Management OPQ — Functional Test Categories for PDMA Compliance
summary: A sample management system used under the Prescription Drug Marketing Act (PDMA) requires specific OPQ test categories covering the drug sample lifecycle. These test categories apply to any Salesforce-based sample management implementation.

delivery_tracking.description: Track periodic sample allocation shipments by warehouse to Sales Representatives
delivery_tracking.pdma_relevance: PDMA Section 353(d) requires manufacturers to maintain records of drug sample distributions

sample_distribution.description: Track samples distributed (dispensed) to healthcare practitioners
sample_distribution.pdma_relevance: PDMA Section 353(d)(1) requires written receipt for each sample delivered

physical_inventory.description: Periodic physical counts and reconciliation of sample inventory
physical_inventory.pdma_relevance: PDMA Section 353(d)(2) requires physical inventories and reconciliation

transfers.pdma_relevance: Transfers must maintain chain of custody and audit trail per PDMA

returns_and_losses.description: Sample returns to warehouse and theft/loss reporting
returns_and_losses.pdma_relevance: PDMA Section 353(d)(3) requires reporting of stolen/falsified samples

reporting.description: Complete and accurate reporting for drug sample exchange
reporting.pdma_relevance: Reporting demonstrates compliance with PDMA record-keeping requirements

audit_trail.description: Verify system maintains complete audit trail per 21 CFR Part 11
audit_trail.pdma_relevance: Part 11 requires secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails

screen_navigation_and_security.description: Verify UI screens are designed correctly and role-based access is enforced
test_areas: Home page elements by user role
Button and action availability by role
screen_navigation_and_security.pdma_relevance: Part 11 requires limiting system access to authorized individuals

multi_product_testing: When the same codebase serves multiple products (e.g., dermatology and aesthetics), all testing scenarios apply to each product line EXCEPT screen navigation, which may differ by product. Execute full OPQ for each product with shared test scripts where applicable.

pre_requisites: Test environment representative of production configuration
Required user profiles and role-based access set up
Test database instance with required dashboards, tables, and views
Populated with test data necessary to facilitate testing (not production data)
ETL processes configured and tested for data load scenarios

gotcha: For sample management specifically, PDMA compliance audits by the FDA Office of Criminal Investigations (OCI) are increasingly common. OCI investigators will request the OPQ protocol and Validation Summary Report specifically for the sample tracking system. Having a well-structured, complete OPQ is not just a regulatory checkbox — it is directly tied to enforcement risk.
